title: Best VPS for OpenClaw: requirements and which KVM plan to pick

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: If the AI model runs at a provider, through your API key or Hostinger's AI credits, KVM 1, with 4 GB, is the starting point. For a local model, the documentation sets an 8 GiB floor, and KVM 4, with 16 GB, is the first plan with room to spare. The count is in How much RAM each scenario needs.

contentSections.heading: What the official documentation says (and does not say) about requirements
paragraphs: OpenClaw is an AI assistant you run on your own server or computer. The model that answers can stay at a provider, reached through your API key or Hostinger's AI credits, or run on the server itself, as a local model. An API key is the password OpenClaw uses to ask a provider such as Anthropic or OpenAI for answers; the provider charges per use. With the model at the provider, the server only runs the program.
The official installation and local-model pages, read on October 21, 2026, say the following:
bullets: **Node version.** OpenClaw needs Node 24.16 or newer, or Node 26.1 or newer. Node is the program that runs OpenClaw, and the npm installation requires one of those versions. The page recommends Node 26. If Node is not installed, the official installer brings it (Node 26 on macOS and Node 24 LTS on Linux).

**Local model.** For the smallest recipe the documentation itself offers, the floor is 8 GiB of host memory, with a 64K context. The page says those floors do not guarantee that the model fits or runs at a useful speed.

**Hostinger VPS.** Hostinger installs OpenClaw on the VPS with Docker, a program that runs each application isolated in its own container. The VPS is a rented virtual server; with root access, you have full control of it.
postParagraphs: The documentation gives no RAM, processor (vCPU) or disk figure for OpenClaw without a local model, and no server minimum for the API key or credits scenario.

One detail on units: 8 GiB is about 8.6 GB. KVM 2 is advertised with 8 GB, which is about 7.5 GiB, a little below the floor, before counting the memory the operating system and Docker use. The documentation does not say whether this difference counts toward the floor.

contentSections.heading: How much RAM each scenario needs
paragraphs: RAM is the server's working memory: the program and, with a local model, the model itself stay there while running. The documentation gives a number only for the local model.

headers: What that means for the plan

postParagraphs: Two details about the local model. The context is the amount of text (tokens, pieces of words) the model reads at once. When less than 20% of the context window is left, OpenClaw warns, with a floor of 8,000 tokens; below 10%, it blocks the reply, with a floor of 4,000 tokens.
None of the KVM plan pages we read lists a graphics card (GPU), and the documentation does not say what speed a local model would reach without one.

**KVM 2 (8 GB).** With an API key, there is room to spare. With a local model, it sits at the floor, with no margin for the operating system.

**KVM 8 (32 GB).** Only makes sense with a larger local model. The documentation does not say how much memory each large recipe needs.

contentSections.heading: VPS, running at home or managed: which scenario needs what
paragraphs: The three paths run the same program, OpenClaw, with different costs and chores. The choice depends on three things: whether you want to deal with a server, whether a computer can stay on 24 hours a day, and whether the AI model runs at a provider or on your own hardware.

rows: You want the assistant running without touching a server, with an API key or Hostinger credits
Hostinger installs and maintains the assistant. On October 21, 2026, US$3.99/month with SONAR20, on a 24-month plan

You have full control. Updates and server security are yours

contentSections.heading: The free VPS: Oracle Always Free
paragraphs: Oracle has a free tier, Always Free. It is not from Hostinger and does not replace the paid VPS, but it is a way to test OpenClaw without paying. According to Oracle's documentation, read on October 21, 2026:
bullets: Up to two Micro instances (AMD processor), with 1/8 OCPU and 1 GB of memory each.
Arm Ampere A1 instances: 2 OCPUs and 12 GB of memory in total, which you split as you like. The monthly limit is 1,500 OCPU-hours and 9,000 GB-hours.
200 GB of block storage in total, for the system disks and extras, with up to five backups.
Free instances must be created in the account's home region. Creating them elsewhere generates charges.
postParagraphs: The rule that matters: Oracle says it can reclaim an idle instance. An instance is idle when, over a 7-day period, CPU usage at the 95th percentile stays below 20%, network usage stays below 20% and, on the A1 instances, memory usage also stays below 20%. An assistant that sits waiting most of the time can fall under this rule. The documentation does not describe a notice before reclamation.

paragraphs: The choice follows where the AI model runs and how much server work you want.

No server to look after: the managed plan, where Hostinger installs and updates the assistant, at US$3.99/month with SONAR20.
Testing for free: Oracle Always Free, knowing Oracle may reclaim an idle instance.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: What is the minimum server for OpenClaw? The official documentation publishes no minimum RAM, CPU or disk; it requires Node 24.16 or newer (or 26.1). With an API key or credits, KVM 1 is the starting point. With a local model, the floor is 8 GiB, and KVM 4 is the first with room to spare.

Can you run OpenClaw without an API key? Yes, with a local model, but then memory becomes the problem: the documentation gives 8 GiB as the floor for its smallest local recipe, with a 64K context, and warns that this does not guarantee the model fits or runs well. With Hostinger's AI credits, you do not need an account with an AI provider, but you pay for usage.

Is Oracle Always Free really free? Yes, as long as the account stays within Always Free: 2 OCPUs and 12 GB on the Arm A1, plus the Micro instances. An instance that stays idle for 7 days, with CPU, network and memory below 20%, can be reclaimed by Oracle.
Mac mini or VPS? It depends on whether the computer can stay on 24 hours a day. If it can, running at home removes the server fee; if it cannot, choose a VPS or the managed plan.
Is there a Hostinger coupon for the OpenClaw VPS? Yes: the code SONAR20, in the coupon field of the cart, gives 20% off the first period, on monthly or annual plans.
